source_records.abstract: The emergence and re-emergence of infectious diseases pose persistent challenges to global health security. Outbreaks such as severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), influenza A(H1N1), Ebola virus disease, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), mpox, avian influenza A(H5N1), and hantavirus infections highlight the need for effective preparedness against emerging infectious threats. The concept of “Disease X” further emphasizes the importance of preparing for unknown pathogens that may cause future epidemics or pandemics. This study aimed to examine major infectious disease outbreaks and assess Türkiye’s preparedness for potential future global outbreaks. A descriptive review design was employed, based on a structured literature search and document analysis of scientific publications and institutional reports. The findings were organized and interpreted using a SWOT framework. The analysis identified healthcare infrastructure, intensive care capacity, digital health systems, and experience gained during the COVID-19 pandemic as potential strengths. However, challenges related to healthcare workforce capacity, zoonotic disease surveillance, public health literacy, coordination across human, animal, and environmental health sectors, and dependence on external sources for certain biotechnological products may constrain preparedness. Climate change, environmental disruption, international travel, migration, and global trade were identified as factors that may influence the emergence and spread of infectious diseases. Strengthening integrated surveillance and early warning systems, improving intersectoral coordination through the One Health approach, enhancing domestic vaccine and diagnostic production capacity, and expanding community-based public health education may help improve Türkiye’s preparedness for future outbreaks. These findings highlight the importance of sustained, multisectoral preparedness for emerging infectious disease threats.

papers.title_zh: SARS、H1N1、EBOLA、COVID-19、MPOX、H5N1 以及 汉坦病毒:人类正进入新一轮大流行时代吗?土耳其为下一次全球疫情做好准备了吗?

analysis_zh.background: 本研究聚焦于SARS、H1N1、Ebola、COVID-19、mpox、H5N1以及 汉坦病毒 等新发和再发传染病的持续挑战,强调针对未知病原体(Disease X)的防备需求。
analysis_zh.methods: 采用描述性综述设计,进行结构化文献检索和对科学出版物及机构报告的文献分析,结果通过SWOT框架进行解读;研究聚焦于土耳其的防备情况,但未报告具体样本量、地点或宿主数据。
analysis_zh.results: 确定的优势包括医疗基础设施、重症监护能力、数字健康系统以及COVID-19的防控经验;挑战涉及医护人员能力、动物源监测、公共卫生素养、部门间协作以及对外部生物技术资源的依赖;气候变化、旅行、迁徙和贸易被视为影响因素;建议强调综合监测、One Health 协调、国产疫苗/诊断产品生产以及社区教育。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本文强调持续的多部门新发传染病防备重要性,并提供了评估国家准备情况的框架,针对土耳其,具有政策和监测策略的启示意义。
analysis_zh.limitations: 在提供的证据中未报告。

papers.title: Cuadro clínico y eventos inmunológicos del síndrome cardiopulmonar por variantes Sudamericanas de Hantavirus: revisión sistemática
papers.abstract: Objetivo. Analizar los mecanismos inmunopatológicos implicados en el desarrollo del HCPS y su correlación con la severidad de las manifestaciones clínicas de las variantes sudamericanas. Métodos. Se realizó una revisión sistemática de la literatura científica sobre la inmunopatogenia de hantavirus sudamericanos bajo los lineamientos PRISMA 2020. Desarrollo. Las variantes de Hantavirus en Bolivia (ANDV, RIOMV y LNV) desencadenan el HCPS. El virus infecta el endotelio sin destruirlo directamente. La variante AND evade la respuesta innata acumulando alta carga viral, mientras RIOMV hiperestimula macrófagos y perfil Th1/Th17. Esto desregula la permeabilidad capilar, causando edema pulmonar no cardiogénico y shock cardiogénico. Conclusiones. El síndrome es una enfermedad inmunomediada donde la severidad depende de la variante genética. El daño tisular no es lítico, sino el resultado de una respuesta inmune descontrolada y una tormenta de citocinas. Comprender esta inmunopatogenia es crucial para diseñar terapias dirigidas a regular la inflamación sistémica.

analysis.background: The paper aims to analyze the immunopathological mechanisms driving hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) and their link to clinical severity of South American hantavirus variants.
analysis.methods: A systematic review of the scientific literature on South American hantavirus immunopathogenesis was performed following PRISMA 2020 guidelines.
analysis.results: Bolivian hantavirus variants (ANDV, RIOMV, LNV) trigger HCPS; the virus infects endothelial cells without direct lysis; ANDV evades innate immunity with high viral load, while RIOMV hyper‑stimulates macrophages and a Th1/Th17 profile; this dysregulates capillary permeability, causing non‑cardiogenic pulmonary edema and cardiogenic shock; disease severity is immunomediated and varies with viral genotype; tissue damage results from an uncontrolled cytokine storm rather than direct viral cytopathy.
analysis.contribution: By synthesizing immunopathogenic data, the review highlights targets for therapies aimed at modulating systemic inflammation in HCPS.
analysis.limitations: Only abstract and partial/full‑text information are available; specific methodological limitations of the included studies are not reported.

analysis.summary_en: Background: The study analyzes immunopathological mechanisms of HCPS and their relation to clinical severity of South American hantavirus variants. Methods: A systematic review was conducted under PRISMA 2020. Results: Bolivian variants (ANDV, RIOMV, LNV) cause HCPS; the virus infects endothelium without lysis; ANDV evades innate immunity, RIOMV hyper‑stimulates macrophages and Th1/Th17 responses, leading to capillary leak, pulmonary edema, and cardiogenic shock; severity depends on viral genotype and cytokine storm. Contribution: The synthesis identifies immunomodulatory therapy targets. Limitations: Only abstract/partial text is available and study‑specific limitations are not reported.

analysis_zh.results: 玻利维亚的汉坦病毒变种(ANDV、RIOMV、LNV)可诱发汉坦病毒心肺综合征;病毒感染内皮细胞但不导致直接裂解;ANDV通过高病毒载量逃避免疫先天防御,而RIOMV则过度刺激巨噬细胞并诱导Th1/Th17型免疫反应;此过程扰乱毛细血管通透性,导致非心源性肺水肿和心源性休克;疾病严重程度为免疫介导,随病毒基因型而异;组织损伤源于失控的细胞因子风暴,而非直接的病毒细胞毒性。
analysis_zh.contribution: 通过综合免疫致病数据,综述指出了针对调节汉坦病毒心肺综合征系统性炎症的治疗靶点。
analysis_zh.limitations: 仅可获得摘要及部分/全文信息;未报告所纳入研究的具体方法学局限性。

papers.title: Epigenetics of HFRS: Linking Immunity, Pathogenesis, and Vaccine-Induced Protection.
papers.abstract: Haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), caused by Old World hantaviruses, including Hantaan virus (HTNV) and Seoul virus (SEOV), is an important public-health concern, particularly in Asia. Clinical manifestations range from febrile illness to vascular leakage, thrombocytopenia, haemorrhage and acute kidney injury. The mechanisms underlying variation in disease severity and the variability and durability of vaccine-induced immunity remain incompletely understood. Epigenetic mechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin regulation and non-coding RNA-mediated regulation, can influence antiviral immunity and immune-cell function in several biological settings; however, their specific contributions to HFRS remain insufficiently characterized. This structured narrative review examines hantavirus-specific evidence alongside relevant findings from other viral infections and vaccination settings, focusing on inflammatory responses, endothelial dysfunction, regulatory non-coding RNAs, trained immunity and potential applications in vaccinology. Experimental HTNV studies and clinical investigations of regulatory RNAs have identified candidate pathways associated with hantavirus-host interactions; however, these findings do not establish that epigenetic mechanisms determine HFRS severity or clinical outcomes. Similarly, preclinical hantavirus vaccine studies and early clinical evaluations provide evidence regarding immunogenicity and safety but do not demonstrate epigenetic mediation of protective immunity. Findings from Andes virus (ANDV), associated primarily with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), and other viral systems are therefore considered comparative or contextual evidence, not directly generalizable to HFRS. This review identifies critical knowledge gaps and outlines how longitudinal, cell-resolved epigenomic profiling, functional validation and integrated multi-omics could clarify causal mechanisms, explain interindividual variation in disease outcomes and vaccine responses, and establish the potential translational value of epigenetic biomarkers and interventions.

analysis.background: HFRS, caused by Old World hantaviruses such as HTNV and SEOV, remains a significant public‑health issue in Asia (A1).
analysis.main_directions: The review focuses on epigenetic regulation of inflammatory responses, endothelial dysfunction, regulatory non‑coding RNAs, trained immunity, and their potential relevance to vaccine design (A6).
analysis.current_state: While epigenetic mechanisms are known to modulate antiviral immunity, their specific role in HFRS severity and vaccine‑induced protection is still incompletely understood (A3).
analysis.gaps: Direct evidence linking particular epigenetic changes to HFRS outcomes or vaccine efficacy is lacking, and the contributions of these mechanisms remain insufficiently characterized (A5).
analysis.future_research: Longitudinal, cell‑type‑resolved epigenomic profiling, functional validation, and integrated multi‑omics are proposed to uncover causal pathways, explain inter‑individual variability, and assess epigenetic biomarkers or interventions (A11).

analysis.summary_en: Background: HFRS caused by HTNV and SEOV is a major Asian health concern (A1). Main directions: The review examines epigenetic control of inflammation, endothelial injury, non‑coding RNAs, trained immunity, and vaccine implications (A6). Current state: Epigenetic influence on antiviral immunity is recognized, yet its specific impact on HFRS severity and vaccine protection is unclear (A3). Gaps: Evidence directly tying epigenetic alterations to disease outcomes or vaccine response is insufficient (A5). Future research: Calls for longitudinal, cell‑specific epigenomic studies, functional assays, and multi‑omics integration to define mechanisms, variability, and translational potential (A11).

papers.title_zh: 肾综合征出血热的表观遗传学:连接免疫、发病机制与疫苗诱导的保护

analysis_zh.background: 肾综合征出血热(HFRS)由旧世界汉坦病毒病毒(如HTNV和SEOV)引起,仍是亚洲的重要公共卫生问题(A1)。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述聚焦于炎症反应的表观遗传调控、内皮功能障碍、调控性非编码RNA、训练性免疫及其在疫苗设计中的潜在关联(A6)。
analysis_zh.current_state: 虽然已知表观遗传机制可调节抗病毒免疫,但其在肾综合征出血热严重程度及疫苗诱导保护中的具体作用仍未完全阐明(A3)。
analysis_zh.gaps: 缺乏将特定表观遗传改变与肾综合征出血热结局或疫苗效力直接关联的证据,这些机制的贡献仍未得到充分表征(A5)。
analysis_zh.future_research: 提出进行纵向、细胞类型分辨的表观基因组分析、功能验证以及整合多组学,以揭示因果通路、解释个体间差异,并评估表观遗传生物标志物或干预措施(A11)。

papers.title: Hantavirus RNA Detection in Small Mammals and Spatial Comparison with Reported Human HFRS Cases in West Kazakhstan Region, 2025
papers.abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a zoonotic disease associated with orthohantaviruses maintained in natural rodent hosts. This study assessed the detection and spatial distribution of hantavirus RNA among small mammals in the West Kazakhstan Region in 2025 and compared rodent surveillance findings with human HFRS occurrence. An observational cross-sectional analytical study was conducted in July and September 2025 in four districts. A total of 343 small mammals were captured and morphologically identified. Lung tissue samples from 329 animals collected in September were examined in 123 pooled testing units, whereas 14 animals collected in July were tested individually. Thus, 137 testing units representing 343 animals were evaluated by real-time and conventional RT-PCR. The minimum infection rate (MIR) was calculated as a descriptive minimum estimate, and a pooled-testing likelihood model was used to account for variation in testing-unit size. Hantavirus RNA was detected in 47/137 testing units, including 45 positive pooled units and two individually positive specimens. Based on 343 individual animals, the descriptive MIR was 13.7%. The model-based individual-level infection probability was estimated at 18.0% (95% profile-likelihood CI: 13.5–23.1%). Positive testing units were observed among the Ural field mouse (Apodemus uralensis), bank vole (Myodes glareolus), and common vole (Microtus arvalis). At the district level, the descriptive MIR ranged from 11.6% in Burlinsky to 19.0% in Chingirlauisky. Sampling sites overlapped spatially with settlements reporting human HFRS cases, including Utvinka, Daryinsk, and Rubezhinskoye; however, spatial coincidence does not establish direct transmission.

analysis.background: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a zoonotic disease associated with orthohantaviruses maintained in natural rodent hosts (A1).
analysis.methods: An observational cross‑sectional analytical study was performed in July and September 2025 in four districts of West Kazakhstan (A3); 343 small mammals were captured and morphologically identified (A4); lung tissues from 329 animals were pooled into 123 testing units and 14 animals were tested individually, yielding 137 testing units evaluated by real‑time and conventional RT‑PCR (A5‑A6); the minimum infection rate (MIR) was calculated and a pooled‑testing likelihood model applied (A7).
analysis.results: Hantavirus RNA was detected in 47 of 137 testing units (45 pooled, 2 individual) (A8); descriptive MIR was 13.7% (A9) and model‑based individual infection probability was 18.0% (95% CI 13.5–23.1%) (A10); positives occurred in Apodemus uralensis, Myodes glareolus, and Microtus arvalis (A11); district MIR ranged from 11.6% to 19.0% (A12); rodent‑positive sites overlapped settlements reporting human HFRS cases (A13), though spatial coincidence does not establish direct transmission (A14).
analysis.contribution: The study provides surveillance evidence linking rodent hantavirus prevalence to human HFRS occurrence, supporting spatial risk assessment in West Kazakhstan (A2, A13).
analysis.limitations: Only an abstract is available, limiting detail; spatial overlap does not prove direct transmission; findings are confined to 2025 sampling (A14, evidence_scope).

analysis.summary_en: Background: HFRS is a zoonotic disease linked to orthohantaviruses in rodents (A1). Methods: Cross‑sectional study in four West Kazakhstan districts (2025) captured 343 mammals; lung tissues pooled (123 units) and 14 tested individually, total 137 units analyzed by RT‑PCR; MIR calculated and pooled‑testing model used (A3‑A7). Results: RNA detected in 47/137 units; descriptive MIR 13.7% and model‑based infection probability 18.0% (95% CI 13.5–23.1%); positives in three vole species; district MIR 11.6–19.0%; rodent positives overlapped human HFRS settlements, but spatial coincidence does not prove transmission (A8‑A14). Contribution: Supplies surveillance data linking rodent infection to human cases, aiding risk mapping (A2, A13). Limitations: Abstract only; spatial overlap not causal; limited to 2025 data (A14).

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 2025年哈萨克斯坦西部地区小型哺乳动物RNA检测及与报告的人类肾综合征出血热病例的空间比较

analysis_zh.background: 肾综合征出血热(HFRS)是一种人畜共患疾病,与在自然啮齿动物宿主中维持的 正汉坦病毒es 相关 (A1)。
analysis_zh.methods: 在2025年7月和9月于哈萨克斯坦西部四个地区 (A3) 开展了一项观察性横断面分析研究;捕获了343只小型哺乳动物并进行形态学鉴定 (A4);将329只动物的肺组织合并为123个检测单元,另有14只动物单独检测,得到共计137个检测单元,使用实时和常规RT‐PCR 进行评估 (A5‐A6);计算了最低感染率(MIR),并应用了合并检测似然模型 (A7)。
analysis_zh.results: 汉坦病毒 RNA 在137个检测单元中检测到47例(其中45个为合并样本,2个为单独样本)(A8);描述性最低感染率(MIR)为13.7% (A9),基于模型的单个感染概率为18.0%(95% CI 13.5–23.1%)(A10);阳性样本出现在乌拉尔田鼠(Apodemus uralensis)、灰田鼠(Myodes glareolus)和草原田鼠(Microtus arvalis)中 (A11);各地区的MIR范围为11.6%至19.0% (A12);带病毒的啮齿动物分布点与报告有人类HFRS病例的定居点重叠 (A13),但空间重合并不证明直接传播 (A14)。
analysis_zh.contribution: 该研究提供了监测证据,将啮齿动物 汉坦病毒 的流行率与人类HFRS的发生关联,支持在哈萨克斯坦西部进行空间风险评估 (A2, A13)。
analysis_zh.limitations: 仅有摘要可用,导致细节受限;空间重叠并不能证明直接传播;研究结果仅限于2025年的采样 (A14, evidence_scope)。

papers.title: Structural basis for protocadherin-1 recognition by New World hantaviruses.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne pathogens that cause severe human disease for which no approved therapeutics are available. New World hantaviruses, including Andes virus (ANDV), use the cell-surface receptor protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) to enter host cells1. However, the structural basis of this interaction remains unclear. Here we describe the structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike at near-atomic resolution. PCDH1 asymmetrically engages a deep central pocket formed by four Gn protomers in the spike, explaining why only intact viral particles or soluble tetramers recognize it. Mutagenesis identified three Gn loops that shape the receptor-binding site and afford the transfer of PCDH1 binding from New World to Old World glycoproteins. Structural and functional analyses of four neutralizing antibodies revealed that they block receptor binding through two distinct mechanisms—occluding access to the PCDH1-binding site or sterically preventing receptor engagement. Together, these findings define the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition, reveal how a virus can mask its receptor-binding site by recessing it in a surface depression and how antibodies can counter this strategy, and provide a framework for the design of antiviral therapeutics targeting the hantavirus spike. The structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike defines the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition.

papers.title: Risk Communication in a Post-Pandemic World: Lessons from the 2026 Andes Virus Outbreak
papers.abstract: In May 2026, a hantavirus outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship triggered public alarm disproportionate to its actual scale, despite the rapid diagnosis, clear WHO and ECDC guidance, and swift containment within three months. This commentary asks why outbreaks that health authorities handle correctly can still produce pandemic-level panic. Drawing on media framing research and the Hondius case itself, there seem to be two forces at work. One is news coverage that foregrounds alarming questions while burying expert reassurances. The second one is that post-pandemic public has learnt to distrust reassurance after Covid, when authorities failed to convey that guidance would evolve. This piece contends that clear, accurate and timely statements from health authorities are no longer sufficient on their own and proposes three practices going forward. Recommendations involve naming and directly addressing alarming narratives early, treating community trust as infrastructure built before a crisis rather than during one, and engaging with social media conversations directly rather than relying solely on content removal. Since it was small and well controlled, this outbreak offers a low-cost opportunity to test these practices before a larger outbreak makes the same communication gap far more costly.

papers.title: Hantaviruses as Emerging Zoonotic Pathogens: Molecular Biology, Epidemiology, Therapeutics, vaccine, and Pathogenesis.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are globally distributed zoonotic pathogens belonging to the family Hantaviridae and are responsible for two major human diseases, hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). Despite substantial progress in hantavirus research, important challenges remain in understanding the interactions among viral evolution, reservoir ecology, environmental change, transmission dynamics, and host immunopathology. This review provides an integrated One Health perspective that connects molecular virology and host-virus interactions with transmission ecology, global epidemiology, and the mechanisms underlying vascular leakage and severe disease. In addition to summarizing established knowledge, we highlight recent advances in hantavirus taxonomy, genomic and molecular surveillance, ecological and transmission modeling, and the identification of hantavirus circulation in previously underrecognized regions. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of reservoir host dynamics, climate and environmental change, habitat disturbance, and human-wildlife interactions in shaping spillover risk, as well as on endothelial dysfunction, immune dysregulation, and coagulation abnormalities as interconnected mechanisms of disease severity. We also identify persistent knowledge gaps concerning host susceptibility, viral persistence, determinants of differential virulence and tissue tropism, interspecies transmission, and the development of effective antiviral therapies and vaccines. By integrating these complementary perspectives, this review provides a framework for understanding hantavirus emergence and pathogenesis while identifying priorities for future surveillance, prevention, and therapeutic research.

analysis.background: Hantaviruses are globally distributed zoonotic agents causing HFRS and HCPS, prompting a review of their emergence and impact.
analysis.main_directions: Key themes include viral evolution, reservoir ecology, environmental change, transmission dynamics, and host immunopathology.
analysis.current_state: The review adopts a One Health framework linking molecular virology, transmission ecology, global epidemiology, and mechanisms of vascular leakage.
analysis.gaps: Critical gaps remain in understanding host susceptibility, viral persistence, virulence determinants, tissue tropism, interspecies transmission, and effective antivirals or vaccines.
analysis.future_research: Priorities are integrated surveillance, ecological modeling, and development of therapeutics and vaccines targeting endothelial dysfunction and immune dysregulation.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Hantaviruses cause HFRS and HCPS worldwide, warranting synthesis. Main directions: The review highlights viral evolution, reservoir ecology, environmental change, transmission, and host immunopathology. Current state: A One Health perspective connects molecular virology, ecology, epidemiology, and vascular leakage mechanisms. Gaps: Knowledge gaps include host susceptibility, persistence, virulence, tissue tropism, interspecies spread, and lack of effective antivirals/vaccines. Future research: Emphasizes integrated surveillance, ecological modeling, and therapeutic/vaccine development targeting endothelial and immune pathways.

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒es 作为新兴的动物源性病原体:分子生物学、流行病学、治疗学、疫苗及发病机制。

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒是全球分布的动物源性病原体,可导致肾综合征出血热(HFRS)和汉坦病毒心肺综合征(HCPS),促使对其出现和影响进行综述。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 关键主题包括病毒进化、储宿主生态、环境变化、传播动力学以及宿主免疫病理学。
analysis_zh.current_state: 本综述采用 One Health 框架,关联分子病毒学、传播生态、全球流行病学以及血管渗漏机制。
analysis_zh.gaps: 在了解宿主易感性、病毒持久性、致病性决定因素、组织嗜性、跨种传播以及有效的抗病毒药物或疫苗方面仍存在关键空白。
analysis_zh.future_research: 优先事项包括综合监测、生态建模,以及针对内皮功能障碍和免疫失调的治疗药物和疫苗研发。

papers.summary_zh: 背景：汉坦病毒是全球分布的动物源性病原体,可导致肾综合征出血热(HFRS)和汉坦病毒心肺综合征(HCPS),促使对其出现和影响进行综述。 主要方向：关键主题包括病毒进化、储宿主生态、环境变化、传播动力学以及宿主免疫病理学。 研究现状：本综述采用 One Health 框架,关联分子病毒学、传播生态、全球流行病学以及血管渗漏机制。 不足：在了解宿主易感性、病毒持久性、致病性决定因素、组织嗜性、跨种传播以及有效的抗病毒药物或疫苗方面仍存在关键空白。 后续研究：优先事项包括综合监测、生态建模,以及针对内皮功能障碍和免疫失调的治疗药物和疫苗研发。

papers.title: Expanded protocadherin-1 usage reveals a broader hantavirus entry landscape.
papers.abstract: Mammalian hantaviruses are RNA viruses that cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in the Americas and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Eurasia. The cellular entry mechanisms of most hantaviruses remain poorly defined. To examine entry by phylogenetically distinct hantaviruses identified across Africa, Eurasia, and the Americas, we generated replication-competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) bearing Gn/Gc proteins from Necoclí, Sangassou, Thottapalayam, Kenkeme, Nova, Oxbow, and Tula viruses. All these Gn/Gc proteins except Kenkeme supported infection of primary human endothelial cells, indicating that endothelial cell entry is permissive for a broader range of hantaviruses than previously appreciated. Except for rVSV-Kenkeme, these rVSVs did not acquire additional mutations beyond pre-engineered rescue-enhancing changes during rescue and passaging. Genetic studies in human cells lacking protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) showed that Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses use PCDH1 for efficient infection, although the Nova phenotype was weaker. These three Gn/Gc proteins bound soluble PCDH1 with different apparent avidities, and infection by the corresponding rVSVs was inhibited by soluble PCDH1; Necoclí and Tula, but not Nova, were also blocked by a PCDH1-targeting monoclonal antibody. Authentic Tula virus infection was similarly reduced in PCDH1 knockout endothelial cells. Finally, the broadly reactive anti-Gn/Gc human monoclonal antibody ADI-42898 efficiently neutralized Necoclí, Nova, Sangassou, and Kenkeme rVSVs, but showed weak or undetectable activity against Oxbow, Tula, and Thottapalayam rVSVs. Together, these findings expand the range of hantavirus glycoproteins capable of mediating infection of human endothelial cells, broaden the phylogenetic scope of PCDH1-dependent entry, and identify receptor-targeted and viral glycoprotein-targeted strategies with differential activity.IMPORTANCEMany newly discovered hantaviruses are known only from sequence data, leaving their ability to enter human cells and their receptor usage unresolved. Using a BSL2-compatible recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) system, we show that glycoproteins from several divergent hantaviruses can mediate infection of primary human endothelial cells, indicating that endothelial cell entry is permissive for a broader range of hantaviruses than previously appreciated. We also show that protocadherin-1 (PCDH1), previously linked mainly to New World hantaviruses, is used by Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses but not universally across the panel, revealing broader but heterogeneous receptor usage. An authentic Tula virus experiment supports this conclusion beyond the surrogate system. Finally, a broadly reactive anti-Gn/Gc antibody neutralizes several, but not all, of these viruses, highlighting both the promise and the limits of broadly protective countermeasures and the utility of these rVSVs for evaluating entry inhibitors.

When humans are accidentally exposed to 63 aerosolized excreta from infected reservoir hosts, rodent-borne hantaviruses can cause 64 severe, often fatal diseases, such as hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) in 65 the Americas and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Europe and Asia(2, 66 3). Periodic hantavirus outbreaks continue to occur, and Andes virus (ANDV) is notable 67 for rare human-to-human transmission in a close-contact setting, such as on the MV 68 Hondius Cruise Ship in April-May 2026(4–7). Despite their significant impact on public 69 health, there are currently no FDA-approved vaccines or therapeutics for hantavirus 70 infections, and our understanding of their entry mechanisms remains poor(2, 8). 71 Studies based on genetic sequencing over the past few decades have discovered 72 many new mammalian hantaviruses carried by rodents, insectivores, and bats(9, 10). 73 Currently, the International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses (ICTV) recognizes 48 74 species of mammalian hantaviruses globally(11). However, for most of these 75 hantaviruses, no virus isolates are available, and their potential to cause human infection 76 and illness remains unknown(12). Additionally, the need for high-level biocontainment 77 (BSL3) in hantavirus research and the lack of a robust reverse genetics systems to study 78 the complete hantavirus infection cycle greatly hinder our understanding of their 79 biology(2). 80 Hantavirus particles carry a negative-sense, tripartite genome composed of small 81 (S), medium (M), and large (L) segments(13). The S segment encodes the nucleoprotein 82 (N), which coats the genome; the L segment encodes the L protein, which possesses 83 Page 5 of 40 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and endoribonuclease activities required for genome 84 replication and transcription, respectively. The M segment encodes the glycoprotein 85 complex as a single polyprotein, which is processed by cellular proteases to generate the 86 Gn and Gc glycoproteins(14). The Gn/Gc heterodimers are arranged in a tetrameric 87 cloverleaf-like structure on hantavirus particles, forming spikes(15). Gn is believed to 88 interact with host receptors, while Gc mediates fusion of the viral and endosomal 89 membranes during cellular entry(2, 15). Because Gn/Gc are necessary and sufficient to 90 mediate cellular entry, vesicular stomatitis viruses carrying Gn/Gc serve as powerful tools 91 for studying viral entry(2, 16). 92 Among proposed hantavirus entry receptors, only protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) has 93 compelling in vivo support; it is required for infection and pathogenesis of ANDV in Syrian 94 hamsters(17, 18). Earlier in vitro studies have implicated β1-3 integrins (ITGβ1, ITGβ2, 95 ITGβ3), decay-accelerating factor (DAF)/CD55, and the globular head of C1q receptor 96 (gC1qR) as potential attachment factors or receptors for hantavirus entry(19–24). 97 However, their in vivo relevance is not clear, and ITGβ1, ITGβ3 and DAF/CD55 are not 98 essential for hantavirus infection in human endothelial cells, the major targets of 99 hantavirus infection(25). Genetic knockout and biochemical studies demonstrated that 100 protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) is required for the entry of 5 species of New World 101 hantaviruses: Andes virus, Sin Nombre virus (SNV), Prospect Hill virus, Maporal virus, 102 and Choclo virus, but not for the Old World hantaviruses such as Hantaan virus (HTNV), 103 Puumala virus, and Seoul virus(18, 25). The first extracellular cadherin (EC1) domain of 104 PCDH1 binds the Gn/Gc of New World hantaviruses, and disruption of the PCDH1:Gn/Gc 105 interaction by complete knockout or point mutations in EC1 protects Syrian hamsters 106 Page 6 of 40 against a lethal Andes virus challenge(17, 18). Moreover, soluble PCDH1 carrying the 107 EC1 domain and the EC1-specific monoclonal antibody (mAb-3305) neutralize rVSV- 108 ANDV and SNV infections(17, 18). However, the extent of PCDH1 usage by distinct 109 hantavirus lineages remains unknown. 110 To capture genetic, geographic, and reservoir-host variation, we focused on shrew- 111 borne Thottapalayam virus (TPMV) and Kenkeme virus (KKMV); mole-borne Nova virus 112 (NVAV), and Oxbow virus (OXBV); New World rodent-borne Necoclí virus (NECV); Old 113 World rodent-borne Sangassou virus (SANGV), and vole-borne Tula virus (TULV)(26). 114 Thottapalayam virus was first isolated from the Asian house shrew in India(27), and 115 Kenkeme virus was identified in the flat-skulled shrew in Russia(28). Nova virus is a highly 116 divergent mole-borne virus of the European mole and was initially detected in Hungary, 117 with high prevalence later documented in France(29, 30). Necoclí virus is principally 118 associated with Cherrie’s cane rat in Colombia(31). Sangassou virus is the first 119 indigenous African hantavirus isolate and was identified in the African wood mouse in 120 Guinea(32). Tula virus is classically associated with common voles and related arvicoline 121 hosts across Eurasia(26, 33). Among these viruses, Sangassou virus entry studies 122 implicated integrin β1 as a receptor(32), whereas Tula virus has the strongest direct 123 evidence of human relevance, with a molecularly confirmed symptomatic infection 124 reported in an immunocompetent patient(34). While serologic evidence suggests possible 125 human exposure to Thottapalayam and Sangassou viruses, the ability of Kenkeme, Nova, 126 Oxbow, and Necoclí viruses to cause human infection or disease remains unknown(35– 127 38). Although their reservoir-host associations are better established, human-cell tropism 128 and receptor usage remain poorly characterized for most of these viruses(26, 38). 129 Page 7 of 40 Together, these phylogenetically divergent hantaviruses associated with a variety of 130 reservoir hosts provide a framework to evaluate human cell-tropism and PCDH1 131 dependence across mammalian hantaviruses. 132 Here, we generated rVSVs expressing the Gn/Gc proteins of the seven genetically 133 and ecologically heterogeneous hantaviruses mentioned above to investigate their entry 134 mechanisms and host receptor usage. Infectivity assays in human cells, including primary 135 endothelial cells, demonstrated that these Gn/Gc, except that of Kenkeme virus, can 136 mediate infection of human cells without acquiring additional adaptive mutations. 137 Experiments with PCDH1 knockout human cells and ELISA-based binding assays 138 demonstrated that Necoclí, Tula, and Nova virus Gn/Gc-mediated infections depend on 139 PCDH1. Finally, we demonstrated the utility of PCDH1 and Gn/Gc-targeting approaches 140 for neutralizing these viral infections. 141 Results 142 Divergent hantavirus Gn/Gc proteins mediate infection of human endothelial cells 143 Hantavirus Gn/Gc sequences are highly divergent across species, with 40-60% amino 144 acid differences between them. Our hantavirus panel was selected to sample viruses 145 spanning diverse reservoir hosts, phylogenetic lineages and geographic origins (Fig. 1). 146 To enable cellular entry studies of these hantaviruses at BSL2, we generated 147 recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) expressing Gn/Gc in place of the native 148 VSV G protein. These viruses also express an enhanced GFP reporter (Fig. 2A, top 149 panel). 150 Because New World hantavirus glycoproteins are more compatible with plasma- 151 membrane budding, whereas Old World hantavirus glycoproteins are typically Golgi- 152 Page 8 of 40 localized, rVSVs bearing New World hantavirus Gn/Gc are generally rescued without 153 adaptive mutations(39, 40). In contrast, Old World hantaviruses, such as Hantaan virus 154 and Dobrava-Belgrade virus, require two mutations, I532K in the cytoplasmic tail of Gn, 155 and S1094L in the membrane-proximal part of the Gc ectodomain, to enhance rVSV 156 generation(16). These mutations are unlikely to directly affect receptor engagement 157 because they were previously shown to enhance rVSV infectivity primarily by altering 158 glycoprotein localization and incorporation into virions(16). Accordingly, we preemptively 159 altered the Gn/Gc sequences of Thottapalayam, Kenkeme, Nova, Oxbow, and 160 Sangassou viruses to incorporate HTNV-adaptive changes for rVSV generation (Fig. 2A, 161 bottom panel). 162 Plasmids encoding cognate rVSV genomes carrying codon-optimized Gn/Gc sequences 163 for expression in human cells were transfected into 293FT cells together with the helper 164 plasmids, and the resulting supernatants were used to infect Huh7.51 cells for viral 165 amplification and stock generation. These viruses reached titers of 5-6 log10 per mL in 166 Huh7.5.1 cells. Sequencing of the Gn/Gc inserts in the rVSV genomes confirmed that 167 none of the rVSVs, except rVSV-Kenkeme, acquired additional mutations beyond the pre- 168 engineered ones. In rVSV-Kenkeme, a G485R mutation, numbered according to the 169 glycoprotein precursor, was detected, although its significance remains unclear. 170 To compare infectivity, we normalized viral input by titrating the rVSVs on permissive 171 Huh7.5.1 cells. These titers were then used to determine the multiplicity of infection (MOI) 172 for infection of primary human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells (HPMECs), a 173 major target cell type for hantavirus infection. HPMECs were infected at an MOI of 1 and 174 fixed 24 hours later to assess eGFP-positive cells. All rVSVs except rVSV-Kenkeme 175 Page 9 of 40 infected these cells, although with varying efficiency (Fig. 2B). For quantitative analysis, 176 we evaluated infection at MOIs of 0.2, 1, and 5 at 8 hours post-infection. At an MOI of 177 0.2, only rVSV-Tula infection was evident (4.68%). At MOIs of 1 and 5, rVSV-Tula (23% 178 and 38%, respectively) and rVSV-Thottapalayam (6% and 18%, respectively) infection 179 was detectable, along with the positive controls rVSV-ANDV and rVSV-HTNV, whereas 180 the remaining viruses were not (Fig. 2C, left panel). 181 Kinetic experiments over 48 hrs at MOIs of 0.2 and 1 (Fig. 2C, middle and right panels, 182 respectively) further supported the higher infectivity of rVSV-Thottapalayam and rVSV- 183 Tula, and also revealed substantial infection by rVSV-Necoclí (18 and 36% at 12 hours, 184 respectively) and rVSV-Nova (32 and 38% at 48 hours, respectively). The other three 185 rVSVs, rVSV-Sangassou, rVSV-Oxbow, and rVSV-Kenkeme, showed much lower 186 infectivity: rVSV-Sangassou peaked at 11%, rVSV-Oxbow at 5%, and rVSV-Kenkeme 187 remained barely detectable (<2%). Three broad kinetic patterns were observed: rVSV- 188 Thottapalayam, rVSV-Nova, and, to a lesser extent, rVSV-Sangassou showed a steady 189 increase over time, similar to rVSV-ANDV and rVSV-HTNV; rVSV-Necoclí and rVSV-Tula 190 showed relatively higher infection with little increase over time; and rVSV-Kekeme and 191 rVSV-Oxbow showed very low infection with no increase over time (Fig. 2C). Together, 192 these results show that most of these divergent hantavirus Gn/Gc proteins can mediate 193 infection of primary human endothelial cells. Except Kenkeme virus, this activity was 194 retained without acquisition of additional mutations beyond the pre-engineered changes 195 during rVSV generation. 196 PCDH1 knockout reduces infection by rVSVs bearing Necoclí, Tula, and Nova virus 197 Gn/Gc-mediated entry 198 Page 10 of 40 We have previously used PCDH1 knockout human osteosarcoma U2OS cells to evaluate 199 PCDH1's role in hantavirus infection(17, 18). To assess PCDH1 usage by these rVSVs, 200 we infected WT U2OS cells, a clonal PCDH1 knockout (KO) U2OS cell line, and PCDH1 201 KO U2OS cells complemented with PCDH1 cDNA with pre-titrated amounts of rVSVs 202 selected to yield 20-30% infection in WT cells, except for rVSV-Kenkeme, for which the 203 target infection level was 10%, and quantified infection 24 hours later (Fig. 3A). As with 204 rVSV-ANDV, our positive control, rVSV-Tula infection was reduced in PCDH1 KO cells, 205 and complementation restored infection. Although rVSV-Necoclí and rVSV-Nova infection 206 was also reduced in PCDH1 KO cells, it was not restored in the complemented U2OS 207 cells. Infection by the other 4 rVSVs was unaffected by PCDH1 status. 208 To verify these results in endothelial cells, we tested the same rVSV infections in human 209 TIME endothelial cells, as in our previous work(25). The results in TIME cells were largely 210 consistent with those in U2OS cells: rVSV-ANDV infection decreased by about 80%; 211 rVSV-Necoclí and rVSV-Tula infection each decreased by about 80%; and rVSV-Nova 212 infection decreased by about 50% in the absence of PCDH1 (Fig. 3B). Importantly, 213 infection of all 4 viruses was restored by PCDH1 complementation in this nonclonal 214 knockout population. In contrast, rVSV-Oxbow, rVSV-Kenkeme, rVSV-Thottapalayam, 215 and rVSV-Sangassou infections were unaffected by PCDH1. These results demonstrate 216 that PCDH1 ablation in human cells reduces infection mediated by Necoclí, Tula, and 217 Nova Gn/Gc. 218 Necoclí, Tula, and Nova Gn/Gc specifically bind to PCDH1 219 To determine whether these Gn/Gc bind PCDH1, we first normalized input rVSVs by 220 measuring the VSV matrix (M) protein by Western blotting (Fig. 3A, top panel). We then 221 Page 11 of 40 used our previously validated ELISA, in which rVSV particles bearing hantavirus Gn/Gc 222 are captured by the soluble EC1-2 (sEC1-2) domain of PCDH1 immobilized on an ELISA 223 plate (17, 18). As with rVSV-ANDV, binding of rVSV-Necoclí to PCDH1 was dose 224 dependent, although of lower avidity (Fig. 4A, bottom panel). Binding of rVSV-Tula and 225 rVSV-Nova was weaker and was detectable only at higher virion inputs (Fig. 4B). 226 We next tested whether the EC1-specific mAb-3305 could block this interaction. 227 Preincubation of sEC1-2-coated plates with mAb-3305 before addition of rVSVs caused 228 a dose-dependent…

papers.title_zh: 扩展的protocadherin-1利用揭示了更广泛的 汉坦病毒 进入格局。

analysis_zh.background: 哺乳动物的 汉坦病毒 是RNA病毒,可导致美洲的 汉坦病毒心肺综合征 和欧亚地区的 肾综合征出血热。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究使用一种符合 BSL2 要求的重组水疱性口炎病毒 (rVSV) 系统,携带来自七种系统发育上不同的 汉坦病毒 的 Gn/Gc 蛋白;在原代人类内皮细胞以及缺失 protocadherin‐1 (PCDH1) 的人类细胞中进行感染实验。使用可溶性 PCDH1、针对 PCDH1 的单克隆抗体以及广谱抗 Gn/Gc 单克隆抗体 (ADI‐42898) 来探讨受体使用情况和中和作用。
analysis_zh.results: 除 Kenkeme 外,所有 Gn/Gc 蛋白均可介导原代人类内皮细胞的感染。Necoclí、Tula 和 Nova 病毒依赖 PCDH1 实现高效感染,其中 Nova 的表型较弱。可溶性 PCDH1 抑制相应 rVSV 的感染,针对 PCDH1 的抗体阻断 Necoclí 和 Tula,但不阻断 Nova。真实的 Tula 病毒在 PCDH1 基因敲除的内皮细胞中感染率下降。ADI‐42898 对 Necoclí、Nova、Sangassou 和 Kenkeme rVSV 具有中和活性,但对 Oxbow、Tula 和 Thottapalayam rVSV 的活性弱或未检测到。
analysis_zh.contribution: 该研究扩大了能够介导人类内皮细胞感染的 汉坦病毒 糖蛋白的范围,拓宽了 PCDH1 依赖性进入的系统发育范围,并展示了针对受体和针对病毒糖蛋白的对策活性差异,凸显 rVSV 在评估进入抑制剂方面的实用价值。
analysis_zh.limitations: 在提供的证据中未报告。

papers.title: An ONT sequencing framework for hantavirus genome assembly, variant analysis, and defective viral genome characterization from whole-segment amplicons
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Orthohantaviruses are zoonotic, tri-segmented negative-sense RNA viruses of rodents and other small mammals that can cause severe human disease. Whole genome sequencing remains difficult because of low viral loads, high sequence diversity, and an inherent instability of the viral L segment. Current tiled amplicon and hybrid-capture approaches do not capture the heterogeneity of virus populations, including defective viral genomes (DVGs), which have never been described for hantaviruses. Here, we present an Oxford Nanopore Technologies sequencing framework based on universal reverse transcription primers targeting the conserved genome termini of orthohantaviruses and a single species-specific primer pair per segment, enabling amplification and sequencing of complete S, M, and L segments. We also developed an accompanying bioinformatic pipeline that performs reference-guided assembly of hantavirus genomes, consensus generation, variant calling, and DVG classification using the newly developed ORCHID classification pipeline. We applied this approach to diverse Puumala virus strains from infected cell cultures and bank voles, to representative Old World and New World orthohantaviruses, and to highly pathogenic New World viruses in vivo. In all cases we were able to accurately reconstruct full hantavirus genomes. Notably, we found that hantavirus populations contain highly abundant DVGs and conserved L segment deletions, whereas the S and M segments remained largely intact. Together, this work provides a low-cost, broadly applicable and easily customisable workflow for hantavirus genomics and reveals DVGs as a previously unrecognized feature of hantavirus populations. IMPORTANCE Hantaviruses cause severe and often fatal human diseases, and their diversity and low viral loads make them hard to sequence, which limits surveillance and outbreak investigation. We describe a simple, universal but customisable, low-cost nanopore sequencing workflow that recovers complete genome segments, including the full-length L segment, from cell culture and animal tissues across the entire Orthohantavirus genus. Using this approach, we report the first evidence of defective viral genomes in hantaviruses. These truncated genomes arise mainly from the L segment, which encodes the viral polymerase, and are formed at conserved genomic regions. Defective viral genomes can modulate viral replication, innate immune activation, and persistence in other viruses. Their presence in hantaviruses raises new questions about polymerase function, tolerance in reservoir hosts, and immune-mediated disease in humans. Our framework offers a practical tool for hantavirus genomics and a foundation for investigating how defective genomes shape hantavirus infection.

Using this approach, we report the first evidence of defective viral genomes in 70 hantaviruses. Defective 72 viral genomes can modulate viral replication, innate immune activation, and persistence 73 in other viruses. Our 75 framework offers a practical tool for hantavirus genomics and a foundation for 76 investigating how defective genomes shape hantavirus infection. 77 3 INTRODUCTION 78 Orthohantaviruses (family Hantaviridae, class Bunyaviricetes) are zoonotic segmented 79 negative-sense RNA viruses that are naturally found in small mammal species, 80 including rodents, shrews, moles and bats (1). Human infections occur primarily through 81 inhalation of aerosolized excreta from infected animal hosts and can cause severe 82 disease, including haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and nephropathia 83 epidemica (NE) caused by Old World hantaviruses primarily in Eurasia and hantavirus 84 cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) caused by New World hantaviruses in the Americas 85 (2, 3). Case fatality rates for hantavirus diseases vary significantly depending on the 86 infecting virus species (4): it ranges from <1% for Puumala virus (PUUV), the causative 87 agent for NE, to up to 15% for HFRS-causing Old World hantaviruses such as Hantaan 88 virus (HTNV) in East Asia and Dobrava-Belgrade virus (DOBV) in eastern Europe, and 89 over 30% for HCPS-causing New World hantaviruses such as Andes virus (ANDV) and 90 Sin Nombre virus (SNV). 91 Hantaviruses have small tripartite negative-sense RNA genomes comprising the small 92 (S), medium (M) and large (L) genome segments, encoding only 4-5 viral proteins (5). 93 The S segment encodes the nucleoprotein (NP) and in some cases a non-structural 94 (NS) protein, the M segment encodes the glycoprotein precursor (GPC) which is co- 95 translationally cleaved into the Gn and Gc glycoproteins, and the L segment encodes 96 the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). The genetic sequence divergence at the 97 amino acid level is significant across the hantavirus family (up to 75%) and even within 98 a species (up to 24%) (6). Low viral RNA copy numbers in clinical and rodent samples, 99 and natural RNA degradation outside of infected hosts makes obtaining complete 100 coverage of hantavirus genomes challenging (7, 8). Current state-of-the-art sequencing 101 approaches include metagenome sequencing, tiled amplicon sequencing and hybrid 102 capture-based sequencing, which all require extensive optimisation and large numbers 103 of probes (9–12). Existing long-read amplicon-based sequencing approaches often 104 include single amplicons for the smaller segments, but to date, there are no established 105 protocols to reliably capture the entire L segment in a single amplicon. In addition, while 106 these methods can provide full genome coverage sequencing and provide consensus 107 sequences of viruses, they do not accurately reflect the genetic makeup of any given 108 virus population. In reality, virus populations are highly heterogeneous and contain large 109 proportions of defective viral genomes (DVGs) consisting of genome truncations, 110 duplications and recombinations (13). However, DVGs have so far never been reported 111 for hantaviruses. 112 Here, we designed a whole segment amplicon-based long-read nanopore sequencing 113 method and an end-to-end bioinformatical analysis pipeline for hantavirus genome 114 assembly, alignment, consensus sequence generation, variant calling and defective 115 viral genome analysis (Fig.1A). This approach minimises required optimisation steps for 116 tiling and hybridization probes and enables a much more accurate depiction of 117 heterogenous virus populations without sacrificing sensitivity or genome coverage. 118 Using this method, we were able to sequence several diverse PUUV strains from both 119 infected cell cultures and from bank voles – their natural host species. In addition, we 120 validated our method using representative members of the whole Orthohantavirus 121 genus and samples obtained from cell cultures and animal tissues. Our sequencing 122 4 approach provides a cost-effective and rapid end-to-end pipeline to analyse hantavirus 123 genomes from environmental, animal and cellular samples. In addition, we provide the 124 first report of hantavirus DVGs and provide a framework for their analysis. 125 126 127 RESULTS 128 A nanopore sequencing and bioinformatics pipeline. Here, we designed a 129 whole segment amplicon-based long-read nanopore sequencing method. Hantavirus 130 RNA is reverse transcribed using universal hantavirus primers that hybridize with the 131 highly conserved 14 nucleotides at the genome termini. Subsequently, each genome 132 segment is amplified in a virus species-specific manner using a single longer primer pair 133 corresponding to the specific genome termini of a virus genome segment. PCR 134 products are then sequenced using Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) long-read 135 sequencing technology. This is followed by a bioinformatical analysis pipeline that 136 includes hantavirus reference-guided genome assembly, genome alignment, consensus 137 sequence generation, variant calling and DVG analysis (Fig.1A). The DVG analysis is 138 performed using the ‘ONT-based Recombination and Copy-back Haplotype 139 Identification for DVGs’ (ORCHID) pipeline which detects recombination events in virus 140 genomes and classifies these as artefacts, deletion, or copy-back events (Fig. 1B). 141 Deletion DVGs (delVGs) are produced when the RdRp dissociates from the genome 142 template during replication, continues reading the template without copying any of it, 143 and then reassociates and starts copying the template further downstream, thus 144 creating an internal deletion of the copied genome (Fig. 1C). Copy-back DVGs (cbVGs) 145 are produced when the RdRp dissociates from the template strand during replication 146 and reengages the nascent product strand as a new template (Fig. 1C). Together, this 147 workflow represents a highly customisable end-to-end sequencing and analysis 148 framework for hantaviruses. 149 150 Establishment of whole hantavirus segment amplification. While amplification 151 of the S and M segments in single amplicons has been achieved before, capturing the 152 entire L segment in one single amplicon has so far proven difficult (10). We utilized the 153 extremely high sequence conservation in the terminal 14 nucleotides of the 5’ and 3’ 154 ends of all three genome segments across the entire Orthohantavirus genus to design 155 universal hantavirus reverse transcription primers for both genomic negative-sense viral 156 RNA (vRNA) and the antigenomic positive-sense complementary RNA (cRNA) (Fig. 157 2A). Primers for amplification of individual segments also contained these highly 158 conserved termini but stretched further into the segments to achieve high specificity for 159 virus species and segments. 160 We established and optimised our virus species- and segment-specific viral genome 161 segment RT-PCR (vgsRT-PCR) method on RNA extracted from a cell-free purified 162 PUUV stock. First, we compared different RT primers and found that the Uni-c14 163 primer, random hexamers and oligo(dT) primers performed poorly and resulted in low or 164 no detectable amplification of PUUV segments (Fig. 2B). This was an expected result, 165 since hantaviruses generally are not thought to contain polyadenylation signals and 166 since the virus stock primarily should be composed of vRNA (14, 15). However, use of 167 5 the vRNA-specific Uni-v14 primer alone or in combination with the cRNA-specific Uni- 168 c14 primer yielded strong full-length amplification of all three PUUV segments. 169 Henceforth, the combination of vRNA- and cRNA-specific RT primers was used. Next, 170 different PCR elongation times and cycle numbers were compared. We observed that 171 for the longer L and M segments, increasing elongation time seemed to slightly increase 172 full-length segment amplification, while no major difference was observed for the S 173 segment (Fig. 2C). Based on these data we selected an elongation time of 3 min as the 174 best balance between sensitivity and overall reaction time. Increasing PCR cycle 175 numbers steadily increased PCR product accumulation in all three segments, with 176 robust product accumulation starting at 30 cycles (Fig 2D). As a compromise between 177 sensitivity, PCR bias and time optimisation, we chose 30 cycles as our default option, 178 with the possibility of increasing cycles to 40 for samples that require higher sensitivity. 179 As a proof-of-concept we also tested whether all segment-specific primers can be 180 combined in a single reaction and confirmed that all PUUV segments were efficiently 181 and equally amplified compared to the single primer pair reactions (Fig. 2E). Sensitivity 182 is important when designing PCR protocols for hantaviruses due to their inherently low 183 RNA copy numbers in infected patients. Using in vitro transcribed PUUV S segment 184 vRNA as a standard, we were able to accurately detect up to 101 RNA copies by RT- 185 qPCR (Fig. 2F) and up to 103 RNA copies by vgsRT-PCR (Fig. 2G). 186 Overall, we established a reproducible and sensitive vgsRT-PCR method for the optimal 187 amplification of whole PUUV segments with a single primer pair per segment. 188 189 Nanopore sequencing of diverse PUUV strains from cell culture. Having 190 established that we can robustly amplify full-length PUUV genomes, we next attempted 191 to sequence and characterise these amplicons from more complex samples by ONT 192 long-read sequencing. To that end, we infected human lung epithelial cells with several 193 different PUUV strains and extracted RNA from infected cells. First, we confirmed and 194 compared the presence of viral RNA by RT-qPCR and found robust – but varying – 195 levels of viral RNA in all samples (Fig.3A). Analysis of vgsRT-PCR products by gel 196 electrophoresis demonstrated clean amplification of the full M and S segments for all 197 PUUV strains (Fig. 3B). However, for the L segment we predominantly observed PCR 198 products of varying shorter lengths, suggesting production of internally truncated DVGs 199 that maintained the conserved segment termini. This was especially pronounced for the 200 PUUV strain BE/Cg/Villers-la-Tour/1/2009 (‘Villers-la-Tour’), BE/Cg/Seloignes/1/2009 201 (‘Seloignes’), BE/Cg/Beaumont/1/2012 (‘Beaumont’), and BE/Cg/Turnhout/1/1985 202 (‘Turnhout’), while RUS/Cg/Kazan/E6/1982 (‘Kazan-E6’) exhibited relatively clean full- 203 length products. Interestingly, while these putative DVGs exhibited strain-specific 204 profiles, the overall size distribution appears similar across all virus strains. 205 Nanopore sequencing of these amplicons demonstrated high levels of sequencing 206 depth across the entire genome (Table 1 and Fig. 3C). The genome coverage was even 207 across the entire genome for the M and S segments for all PUUV strains, confirming our 208 previous vgsRT-PCR data. Accordingly, we observed a striking reduction in genome 209 coverage in the central regions of the L segment for all strains except Kazan-E6, which 210 also did not generate any major truncated PCR products. We used the ORCHID 211 pipeline to classify sequenced viral reads and confirmed our vgsRT-PCR and genome 212 6 coverage data: while the M and S segments only contained small fractions of putative 213 and high-confidence DVGs, the vast majority of L segment reads were classified as 214 delVGs (Table 1 and Fig. 3D). Only Kazan-E6 exhibited a lower – yet still significant – 215 fraction of DVGs, consistent with our previous findings. As the M and S segments did 216 not exhibit any meaningful levels of DVGs, and cbVGs could not be detected at 217 significant levels in any segment, we characterized only L segment delVGs further. 218 Analysis of L segment delVG junction sizes revealed a now familiar pattern: while 219 Kazan-E6 only showed few unique junctions that were concentrated between 3000 and 220 4000 nt in size, all the remaining strains almost exclusively had very large 221 (approximately 4000 to 6000 nt in size) deletions (Fig. 3E). This helps explain why we 222 previously observed a relatively uniform pattern of truncated PCR products (Fig. 3B). 223 Investigation of the exact junction sites – i.e. at what nucleotide position of the genome 224 the RdRp disengages from the template (junction start) and then subsequently 225 reengages again (junction end) – helps shed further light onto the nature of these DVGs 226 and reveals highly specific regions in the PUUV L segment that are associated with 227 delVG formation (Fig. 3F). For the Turnhout, Beaumont, Seloignes and Villers-la-Tour 228 strains we observed highly similar patterns: the majority of deletions start within the first 229 100 nt of the 5’ end of the L segment and span almost the entire segment and end 230 within a more variable (approximately 1500 nt) window at the 3’ end of the segment 231 (Fig.3F). 232 Together, these data demonstrated that our whole segment amplicon sequencing 233 method is able to robustly sequence and resolve entire PUUV genomes. Twohig2, Anne Tuiskunen Bäck3,4,5,6, Magnus 5 Sjöblom7, Rebecca Lantto3, Gabriella Svala7, Janne Tynell8,9, Sandra Broddesson10,11, 6 Robert Dyrdak10,11, Wanda Christ1, Silke Riesle-Sbarbaro12, Joseph B. Prescott12, 7 Steven B. Bradfute2, Daniel P. Depledge13,14,15, Benjamin E. Nilsson-Payant1 8 9 1 Division of Virology and Immunology, Department of Microbiology, Tumor and Cell 10 Biology, Karolinska Institutet, Stockholm, Sweden 11 2 Department of Internal Medicine, Center for Global Health, University of New Mexico 12 Health Sciences Center, Albuquerque, New Mexico, United States of America 13 3 Department of Clinical Microbiology, Umeå University, Umeå, Sweden 14 4 Department of Public Health and Clinical Medicine, Umeå University, Umeå, Sweden 15 5 Umeå Centre for Microbial Research (UCMR), Umeå University, Umeå, Sweden 16 6 Laboratory for Molecular Infection Medicine Sweden (MIMS), Umeå University, Umeå, 17 Sweden 18 7 Clinical Microbiology Unit, Department of Laboratory Medicine, Sunderby Hospital, 19 Luleå, Sweden 20 8 Department of Virology, University of Helsinki, Helsinki, Finland 21 9 Institute of Biomedicine, University of Turku, Turku, Finland 22 10 Division of Clinical Genomics & Virology, Department of Microbiology, Tumor and Cell 23 Biology, Karolinska Institutet, Stockholm, Sweden 24 11 Department of Clinical Microbiology, Karolinska University Hospital, Stockholm, 25 Sweden 26 12 Center for Biological Threats and Special Pathogens, Robert Koch Institute, Berlin, 27 Germany 28 13 Institute of Virology, Hannover Medical School, Hannover, Germany 29 14 Cluster of Excellence RESIST (EXC 2155), Hannover Medical School, Hannover 30 Germany 31 15 German Center for Infection Research (DZIF), partner site Hannover-Braunschweig, 32 Hannover, Germany 33 34 35 Corresponding author: benjamin.nilssonpayant@ki.se 36 37 38 39 40 2 ABSTRACT 41 Orthohantaviruses are zoonotic, tri-segmented negative-sense RNA viruses of rodents 42 and other small mammals that can cause severe human disease. Whole genome 43 sequencing remains difficult because of low viral loads, high sequence diversity, and an 44 inherent instability of the viral L segment. Current tiled amplicon and hybrid-capture 45 approaches do not capture the heterogeneity of virus populations, including defective 46 viral genomes (DVGs), which have never been described for hantaviruses. Here, we 47 present an Oxford Nanopore Technologies sequencing framework based on universal 48 reverse transcription primers targeting the conserved genome termini of 49 orthohantaviruses and a single species-specific primer pair per segment, enabling 50 amplification and sequencing of complete S, M, and L segments. We also developed an 51 accompanying bioinformatic pipeline that performs reference-guided assembly of 52 hantavirus genomes, consensus generation, variant calling, and DVG classification 53 using the newly developed ORCHID classification pipeline. We applied this approach to 54 diverse Puumala virus strains from infected cell cultures and bank voles, to 55 representative Old World and New World orthohantaviruses, and to highly pathogenic 56 New World viruses in vivo. In all cases we were able to accurately reconstruct full 57 hantavirus genomes. Notably, we found that hantavirus populations contain highly 58 abundant DVGs and conserved L segment deletions, whereas the S and M segments 59 remained largely intact. Together, this work provides a low-cost, broadly applicable and 60 easily customisable workflow for hantavirus genomics and reveals DVGs as a 61 previously unrecognized feature of hantavirus populations. 62 63 IMPORTANCE 64 Hantaviruses cause severe and often fatal human diseases, and their diversity and low 65 viral loads make them hard to sequence, which limits surveillance and outbreak 66 investigation. We describe a simple, universal but customisable, low-cost nanopore 67 sequencing workflow that recovers complete genome segments, including the full-length 68 L segment, from cell culture and animal tissues across the entire Orthohantavirus 69 genus. Using this approach, we report the first evidence of defective viral genomes in 70 hantaviruses. These truncated genomes arise mainly from the L segment, which 71 encodes the viral polymerase, and are formed at conserved genomic regions. Defective 72 viral genomes can modulate viral replication, innate immune activation, and persistence 73 in other viruses. Their presence in hantaviruses raises new questions about polymerase 74 function, tolerance in reservoir hosts, and immune-mediated disease in humans. Our 75 framework offers a practical tool for hantavirus genomics and a foundation for 76 investigating how defective genomes shape hantavirus infection. 77 3 INTRODUCTION 78 Orthohantaviruses (family Hantaviridae, class Bunyaviricetes) are zoonotic segmented 79 negative-sense RNA viruses that are naturally found in small mammal species, 80 including rodents, shrews, moles and bats (1). Human infections occur primarily through 81 inhalation of aerosolized excreta from infected animal hosts and can cause severe 82 disease, including haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and nephropathia 83 epidemica (NE) caused by Old World hantaviruses primarily in Eurasia and hantavirus 84 cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) caused by New World hantaviruses in the Americas 85 (2, 3). Case fatality rates for hantavirus diseases vary significantly depending on the 86 infecting virus species (4): it ranges from <1% for Puumala virus (PUUV), the causative 87 agent for NE, to up to 15% for HFRS-causing Old World hantaviruses such as Hantaan 88 virus (HTNV) in East Asia and Dobrava-Belgrade virus (DOBV) in eastern Europe, and 89 over 30% for HCPS-causing New World hantaviruses such as Andes virus (ANDV) and 90 Sin Nombre virus (SNV). 91 Hantaviruses have small tripartite negative-sense RNA genomes comprising the small 92 (S), medium (M) and large (L) genome segments, encoding only 4-5 viral proteins (5). 93 The S segment encodes the nucleoprotein (NP) and in some cases a non-structural 94 (NS) protein, the M segment encodes the glycoprotein precursor (GPC) which is co- 95 translationally cleaved into the Gn and Gc glycoproteins, and the L segment encodes 96 the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). The genetic sequence divergence at the 97 amino acid level is significant across the hantavirus family (up to 75%) and even within 98 a species (up to 24%) (6). Low viral RNA copy numbers in clinical and rodent samples, 99 and natural RNA degradation outside of infected hosts makes obtaining complete 100 coverage of hantavirus genomes challenging (7, 8). Current state-of-the-art sequencing 101 approaches include metagenome sequencing, tiled amplicon sequencing and hybrid 102 capture-based sequencing, which all require extensive optimisation and large numbers 103 of probes (9–12). Existing long-read amplicon-based sequencing approaches often 104 include single amplicons for the smaller segments, but to date, there are no established 105 protocols to reliably capture the entire L segment in a single amplicon. In addition, while 106 these methods can provide full genome coverage sequencing and provide consensus 107 sequences of viruses, they do not accurately reflect the genetic makeup of any given 108 virus population. In reality, virus populations are highly heterogeneous and contain large 109 proportions of defective viral genomes (DVGs) consisting of genome truncations, 110 duplications and recombinations (13). However, DVGs have so far never been reported 111 for hantaviruses. 112 Here, we designed a whole segment amplicon-based long-read nanopore sequencing 113 method and an end-to-end bioinformatical analysis pipeline for hantavirus genome 114 assembly, alignment, consensu…

analysis.background: Orthohantaviruses are zoonotic, tri‑segmented negative‑sense RNA viruses of rodents and other small mammals that can cause severe human disease, but whole‑genome sequencing is hampered by low viral loads, high sequence diversity, and instability of the L segment.
analysis.methods: The authors developed an Oxford Nanopore Technologies workflow using universal reverse‑transcription primers targeting conserved genome termini and a single species‑specific primer pair per segment to amplify complete S, M, and L segments, coupled with a reference‑guided bioinformatic pipeline (ORCHID) for assembly, consensus generation, variant calling, and defective viral genome (DVG) classification; the approach was applied to diverse Puumala virus strains from cell culture, bank voles, and representative Old World and New World hantaviruses.
analysis.results: In all tested samples the framework accurately reconstructed full hantavirus genomes and revealed that hantavirus populations contain highly abundant DVGs, predominantly conserved deletions in the L segment, while the S and M segments remained largely intact.
analysis.contribution: The study provides a low‑cost, broadly applicable, and easily customisable nanopore sequencing workflow for the entire Orthohantavirus genus and reports the first evidence of DVGs in hantaviruses, highlighting a previously unrecognised feature with potential implications for surveillance and understanding of viral pathogenesis.
analysis.limitations: The abstract and partial text do not report detailed quantitative performance metrics, validation on clinical specimens, or potential biases of the method; only pre‑print data are presented.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Orthohantaviruses cause severe disease but are hard to sequence due to low loads and L‑segment instability. Methods: An ONT workflow with universal RT primers and a species‑specific primer pair per segment, plus the ORCHID pipeline, was applied to diverse PUUV strains and other hantaviruses. Results: Full genomes were accurately reconstructed and abundant L‑segment defective viral genomes were identified, while S and M segments stayed intact. Contribution: This low‑cost, universal workflow enables hantavirus genomics across the genus and reveals DVGs as a new feature, informing surveillance and pathogenesis studies. Limitations: Quantitative performance, clinical validation, and bias assessment are not reported; findings are from a preprint.

papers.title_zh: 一种基于ONT测序的框架,用于从全段扩增子中进行汉坦病毒基因组组装、变异分析及缺陷病毒基因组表征

analysis_zh.background: 正汉坦病毒es 是源自动物的、三分段负义 RNA 病毒,来自啮齿类和其他小型哺乳动物,可导致严重人类疾病,但全基因组测序受低病毒载量、高序列多样性和 L 段不稳定性的影响。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者开发了一个使用 Oxford Nanopore Technologies 的工作流程,采用针对保守基因组末端的通用逆转录引物,以及每个分段的单一物种特异性引物对,以扩增完整的 S、M 和 L 分段,并结合参考引导的生物信息学管道(ORCHID)进行组装、共识生成、变异检测和缺陷病毒基因组(DVG)分类;该方法已应用于来自细胞培养、旱獾以及代表性旧世界和新世界 汉坦病毒es 的多样化 普马拉病毒 病株。
analysis_zh.results: 在所有测试样本中,该框架准确重建了完整的 汉坦病毒 基因组,并揭示 汉坦病毒 群体中存在大量 DVG,主要是 L 分段的保守缺失,而 S 和 M 分段基本保持完整。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本研究为整个 正汉坦病毒 属提供了低成本、广泛适用且易于定制的纳米孔测序工作流程,并首次报告了 汉坦病毒es 中的 DVG,突显了此前未被认识的特征,对监测和理解病毒致病机制具有潜在意义。
analysis_zh.limitations: 摘要和部分文本未报告详细的定量性能指标、临床样本验证或方法的潜在偏差;仅呈现了预印本数据。

papers.title: Vascular Programs in Emerging and Re-Emerging RNA Virus Infections: Comparative Lessons from SARS-CoV-2, Flaviviruses, and Hantaviruses
papers.abstract: Emerging and re-emerging RNA viruses frequently present with clinical phenotypes that extend beyond classical organ tropism and include vascular leakage, platelet dysregulation, coagulation imbalance, microvascular injury, and thromboinflammation. SARS-CoV-2, flaviviruses, and hantaviruses provide three complementary models of virus-induced vascular disease. This narrative review compares these viruses through a shared endothelial–coagulative framework and proposes four partially overlapping vascular programs: endothelial activation, endothelial barrier failure, coagulation activation, and platelet quantitative or qualitative dysfunction. These programs are intended as a conceptual synthesis of convergent clinical, pathological, and experimental evidence rather than as a quantitative classification system. The framework is used not only to organize known mechanisms, but also to generate testable predictions for cross-virus biomarker panels, organ-specific endothelial models, and phenotype-guided clinical studies. Severe COVID-19 illustrates inflammation-driven endothelial activation, platelet–leukocyte interactions, complement amplification, NETosis, and immunothrombosis. Within the flavivirus group, DENV is used as the principal model for systemic vascular leakage, thrombocytopenia, and hemorrhagic risk; selected non-dengue flaviviruses illustrate how shared endothelial, platelet, and coagulation modules are redirected toward placental dysfunction (ZIKV), neuroinvasion (WNV and JEV), or hepatic failure and coagulopathy (YFV). Hantavirus infections provide a distinctive model of capillary leak syndrome in which non-lytic endothelial infection, immune-mediated injury, and permeability signaling converge on renal and pulmonary microvascular beds. A comparative view suggests that thrombotic, hemorrhagic, and leaky phenotypes are not mutually exclusive categories, but different outcomes of overlapping vascular programs shaped by viral tropism, vascular-bed specialization, immune activation, and host susceptibility.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Emerging RNA viruses often cause vascular complications beyond organ tropism. Main directions: The review uses SARS‑CoV‑2, flaviviruses, and hantaviruses to define four overlapping vascular programs: endothelial activation, barrier failure, coagulation activation, and platelet dysfunction. Current state: These programs explain thrombotic, hemorrhagic, and leaky phenotypes as outcomes of shared endothelial–coagulative pathways influenced by viral tropism and host factors. Future research: Future work should test the proposed biomarker panels, develop organ‑specific endothelial models, and design phenotype‑guided clinical studies across viruses.

papers.title_zh: 新发与再发RNA病毒感染中的血管程序:来自SARS‐CoV‐2、黄病毒及汉坦病毒的比较经验

analysis_zh.background: 新发RNA病毒常在器官特异性之外导致血管并发症。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述以SARS‐CoV‐2、黄病毒和汉坦病毒es为例,界定四个相互重叠的血管程序:内皮激活、屏障失效、凝血激活和血小板功能障碍。
analysis_zh.current_state: 这些程序解释了血栓、出血和渗漏表型,视为受病毒嗜性和宿主因素影响的共同内皮‐凝血通路的结果。
analysis_zh.gaps: 该框架仍属概念性,缺乏定量分类;跨病毒生物标志物面板和器官特异性内皮模型尚未验证。
analysis_zh.future_research: 未来工作应检验所提出的生物标志物面板,构建器官特异性内皮模型,并设计跨病毒的表型导向临床研究。

papers.summary_zh: 背景：新发RNA病毒常在器官特异性之外导致血管并发症。 主要方向：本综述以SARS‐CoV‐2、黄病毒和汉坦病毒es为例,界定四个相互重叠的血管程序:内皮激活、屏障失效、凝血激活和血小板功能障碍。 研究现状：这些程序解释了血栓、出血和渗漏表型,视为受病毒嗜性和宿主因素影响的共同内皮‐凝血通路的结果。 不足：该框架仍属概念性,缺乏定量分类;跨病毒生物标志物面板和器官特异性内皮模型尚未验证。 后续研究：未来工作应检验所提出的生物标志物面板,构建器官特异性内皮模型,并设计跨病毒的表型导向临床研究。

papers.title: Can Hantavirus cruise into the next pandemic?
papers.abstract: Despite concerns arising from a recent ship-associated outbreak on the M/V Hondius cruise, current evidence suggests that Andes virus (ANDV) poses a low pandemic risk. Nevertheless, viral evolution, ecological changes, and reservoir host dynamics could drive future emergence of ANDV, underscoring the need for improved surveillance, diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccine preparedness.
